steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: The incarnation is the Christian belief that God became human in the person of Jesus Christ. "Incarnation" means "made flesh" — from the Latin "caro" (flesh). | Exam Tip: Be prepared to explain why the incarnation matters — it enables salvation (Jesus could bridge the gap between God and humanity), reveals God's nature, and shows God understands human suffering. | RS Exam Tips — The Incarnation: 1. For The Incarnation questions, always include specific scriptural or source references where relevant 2. Explain both religious and non-religious viewpoints 3. Use specialist vocabulary precisely (e.g. terms from the specification) 4. Evaluate by analysing strengths and weaknesses of different views before reaching your conclusion 5.
